r.name: Monarch's Way
r.description: approximate route of Charles II's escape

r.name: Grand Union Canal Walk
r.description: Birmingham to Napton section

r.name: North Birmingham Walking and Cycling Route
r.description: Route 535 is a small cycle route from National Cycle Route 5 in Birmingham City Centre to Gravelly Hill, which carries on for a short way along the Tame Valley Canal

r.name: Ward End Route
r.description: Signposted as 'Ward End Route'.

r.name: Millennium Way (Warks)
r.description: A 100 mile long distance footpath, across the centre of England from Pershore to Chipping Warden via Meriden.

r.name: Jewellery Quarter Heritage Trail
r.operator: Birmingham City Council;Birmingham Museums;Jewellery Quarter Development Trust
r.description: Birmingham’s famous Jewellery Quarter is very unique, no other historic townscape is like it worldwide. Rich in heritage yet still a living, working community. This trail introduces the Quarter’s past and encourages visitors to discover more.

r.name: Rea Valley Route
r.description: NCN 5 section of Rea Valley Route

r.name: Jewellery Quarter Pop Up Cycle Route
3 Parks Cycle Route- Silver Route (Airport Viewing Area to Meriden Park)
r.description: The all-weather route follows the valley of the Hatchford, Westley and Kingshurst Brooks whilst passing through an attractive mixture of formal parkland, wooded areas and open grassland.

r.name: Redditch Cycle Route 17
r.description: From Abbey Stadium, through Abbeydale, Church Hill, Winyates, Matchborough, to Washford - mostly following the Bus Lane.

r.name: Redditch Cycle Route 14
r.description: From Crabbs Cross, Oakenshaw, Greenlands, Ipsley, Washford, Matchborough, to Mappleborough Green. A mixture of roads, paths, and paved bridleways.

r.name: Bromsgrove-Redditch Cycle Route 24
r.description: From Bromsgrove Station to Redditch Station. Follows mostly open countryside on road.

r.name: Galton Valley Health Walk
r.description: Self-guided health walk through Black Country Millenium Urban Forest sites. Route follows what was once the longest earthwork in the world and under Telford's Galton Bridge. Difficulty: Medium due to unsurfaced paths and steps Duration: 45-60 mins

r.name: Warley Woods History Trail
r.description: Self-guided tour of the historical features within Warley Woods- initially landscaped by Samuel Galton in the 1790s.

r.name: Handsworth & Lozells Places of Worship Heritage Trail
r.description: Trail around Handsworth and Lozells- a culturally diverse area, where you can learn about the rich variety of religious communities who live alongside one another in a relatively small area.

r.name: Smethwick Places of Worship Heritage Trail
r.description: A trail around Smethwick- a culturally diverse area where you can learn about the wide variety of religious communities who live alongside one another in a relatively small area.

r.name: Revolution Walk
r.description: The Revolution Walk celebrates three eras of transport: canals, roads and railway. Enjoy the mix of nature and heritage as you venture out of the city along this lush stretch.

r.name: Birmingham Wellbeing Walk: Livery Street to The Mailbox
r.description: With 100+ miles of waterways, Birmingham is the heart of Britain’s canals. Modern architecture meets the canal here in a lovingly regenerated setting. The canal is waiting quietly, away from the urban flurry.

r.name: Manufacturing & Migration Walk
r.description: Since the Middle Ages, central Birmingham has been subject to constant change. On this walk learn about the latest wave of redevelopment and regeneration. See how the city’s heritage is celebrated in converted old and spectacular new buildings.

r.name: Lunar Society Birmingham Heritage Trail
r.description: The purpose of this trail is to enable residents and visitors to learn more about the Lunar Society and 18th-century Birmingham by following in its members’ footsteps. Duration: 1-2 hours

r.name: Bourn Brook Walkway
r.description: Walking route along the Bourn Brook from near to the University of Birmingham to Woodgate Valley

r.name: Bournville Heritage Walk
r.description: Walk around the Cadbury Bournville factory site and the surrounding area exploring the history of the development of Bournville by the Cadbury family.

r.name: Factory Junction to Ladywood Junction
r.description: Cycle along The New Main Line and follow the signs for The National Cycle Route, which takes you to Ladywood Junction and on into Birmingham City Centre. Distance: 6 miles/10 km (approx) Duration: 60 min (approx)

r.name: Walk Smethwick Heritage Trail
r.description: Heritage trail around Smethwick, once known as “the level land where cows graze” from Anglo-Saxon farms Canals fueled a boom, making steam engines, stained glass, ceramics & lighthouses. Historically known as “the workshop of the world.”

r.name: Rail Trail: Wythall > Shirley
r.operator: Heart of England Community Rail Partnership
r.description: A 3-mile wander through the pasture and meadows around the outer Shirley suburbs of Major’s Green and Hollywood. Eyes peeled for the Iron Age hillfort! Duration: 1.5 hours Distance: 3 miles

r.name: Rail Trail: Shirley > The Lakes
r.operator: Heart of England Community Rail Partnership
r.description: A 3-mile trail following the towpath along the Stratford-upon-Avon canal, across Christmas tree plantations, farmland and forests to reach Earlswood Lakes. Duration: 3 hours Distance: 5 miles

r.name: Rail Trail: The Lakes > Earlswood
r.operator: Heart of England Community Rail Partnership
r.description: A 3-mile trail tranquil and easy route, circumnavigating Earlswood Lakes before heading into the leafy shade of Clowes Wood en-route to Earlswood. Duration: 2 hours Distance: 4 miles

r.name: Rail Trail: Earlswood > Wythall
r.operator: Heart of England Community Rail Partnership
r.description: A 1.75-mile short and easy route to Earlswood passing through farm and heathland, crossing the River Cole, and skirting Fulford Golf Course. Duration: 1 hour Distance: 1.75 miles

r.name: Rail Trail: Olton > Shirley
r.operator: Heart of England Community Rail Partnership
r.description: An 8-mile longer meander along the banks of the Grand Union Canal and the River Cole, through the heart of Tolkein Country! Duration: 3.5 hours Distance: 8 miles

r.name: Rail Trail: Whitlocks End > Shirley
r.operator: Heart of England Community Rail Partnership
r.description: A 1.75-mile short and sweet ramble across fields, through Christmas Trees(!) and over the Stratford-upon-Avon Canal to Shirley. Duration: 1 hour Distance: 1.75 miles

r.name: Rail Trail: Wood End Circular
r.operator: Heart of England Community Rail Partnership
r.description: A 2.5-mile easy circular route through some beautiful Warwickshire countryside and the picture perfect village of Tanworth-in-Arden. Duration: 1 hour Distance: 2.5 miles

r.name: Rail Trail: Danzey Circular
r.operator: Heart of England Community Rail Partnership
r.description: A 2.7-mile exceedingly rural ramble from the hamlet of Danzey Green out to the bluebells and southerly views of Mockley Wood. Duration: 1.5 hours Distance: 2.7 miles

r.name: Rail Trail: Henley-in-Arden Circular
r.operator: Heart of England Community Rail Partnership
r.description: A 2.5-mile exceedingly rural ramble from the hamlet of Danzey Green out to the bluebells and southerly views of Mockley Wood. Duration: 2.5 hours Distance: 5.5 miles

r.name: Rail Trail: Wootton Wawen > Wilmcote
r.operator: Heart of England Community Rail Partnership
r.description: A 2.5-mile trail exploring Warwickshire’s oldest church, England’s longest iron aqueduct and enjoying some unparalleled views along the Stratford-upon-Avon Canal. Duration: 2.5 hours Distance: 4.5 miles

r.name: Rail Trail: Wilmcote > Wootton Wawen
r.operator: Heart of England Community Rail Partnership
r.description: A 5.5-mile walk with Shakespearean connections, meandering from Wilmcote along the banks of the River Alne to Wootton Wawen. Duration: 3 hours Distance: 5.5 miles

r.name: Rail Trail: Dorridge > Lapworth
r.operator: Heart of England Community Rail Partnership
r.description: A 5.5-mile gentle wander through wealthy suburbia, along country lanes and onto the peace and tranquillity of the Grand Union Canal towpath to Lapworth. Duration: 2.5 hours Distance: 4.5 miles

r.name: Rail Trail: Widney Manor > Dorridge
r.operator: Heart of England Community Rail Partnership
r.description: A 2.75-mile easy walk through Solihull’s suburbia and countryside between two stations, crossing the M42 and the river Blythe. Duration: 1.5 hours Distance: 2.75 miles

r.name: Rail Trail: Solihull Circular (via Malvern & Brueton Park)
r.operator: Heart of England Community Rail Partnership
r.description: A 5.5-mile walk from Solihull station visitng the town centre, passing through two beautiful local parks and following a stretch of the River Blythe. Duration: 3 hours Distance: 5.5 miles

r.name: Rail Trail: Birmingham International > Marston Green
r.operator: Heart of England Community Rail Partnership
r.description: A 4-mile walk discovering wildflower meadows, oak woodland and parkland along Low Brook on an easy route to Marston Green. Plane spotting optional! Duration: 1.5 hours Distance: 4 miles

r.name: Rail Trail: Marston Green Circular via Elmdon
r.operator: Heart of England Community Rail Partnership
r.description: A 5.5-mile walk to discover a different side of suburban life, with a trail packed with plane spotting, heritage and a surprising amount of green space! Duration: 2.5 hours Distance: 5.5 miles

r.name: Bearwood Beer Mile
r.description: Dare you attempt the Bearwood Beer Mile? Whether you like craft hazy IPA, real ale, summery cider or fighty lager, there is something for all tastes! 🍻We have measured the distance of a route between all nine pubs and it clocks in at 1.4 miles.

r.name: Birmingham Platinum Jubilee Walkway
r.operator: Birmingham City Council;University of Birmingham;Canal and River Trust;West Midlands Combined Authority;Commonwealth Games Federation
r.description: A circular walkway to celebrate Queen Elizabeth II's Platinum Jubilee marked by pavement bronze plaques at 20 points of special significance to the people of Birmingham. Unveiled by HRH The Earl of Wessex.

r.name: Colmore Art Trail
r.description: Art walk by Colmore BID celebrating the rich mix of public art in the business district. The trail showcases a diverse range of sculptures, installations, and architectural highlights, reflecting the city's industrial heritage and its creative present.
